preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or have gained ownership)
The contract must have some bonus pool balance (dayPoolBouns[yesToday] > 0)

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call sumBounsPiece() with a very large number (e.g., type(uint256).max / eachPiece) for the current day's date string (yesToday). This will set dayPoolBounsPiece[yesToday] to an extremely high value. Then, when any user calls receiveBounsToken(), the _sumCanGetToken() function will attempt to subtract dayPoolBounsPiece[yesToday].mul(balancePiece) from dayPoolBouns[yesToday], causing an arithmetic underflow and reverting the transaction. This effectively locks all bonus distributions.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has owner-only functions that can arbitrarily set the dayPoolBounsPiece value. The owner can call sumBounsPiece() to set dayPoolBounsPiece[yesToday] to any value, potentially making it larger than dayPoolBouns[yesToday]. This violates the expected invariant that dayPoolBounsPiece should be derived from the pool balance and market total token.
attempts.attack_strategy: Impersonate the owner and call sumBounsPiece() with a very high value to make dayPoolBounsPiece[yesToday] > dayPoolBouns[yesToday].
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get the current owner address from the contract. 2. Impersonate the owner using vm.prank(). 3. Get yesterday's date string using getDays(). 4. Call sumBounsPiece() with a very large number (e.g., 1e18). 5. Verify that dayPoolBounsPiece[yesToday] > dayPoolBouns[yesToday].
